title: bug: ps1 unchanged-tree 'nothing' landing sends record_commit without skipped/contested, so held contested paths raise no #governors MOE_CONTESTED_HELD alert
description:
scripts/moe-agent.ps1 has two gaps against sh, whose record_commit_rpc always sends skipped and contested:
- The `-not $built.Changed` branch (~line 4785, MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT) calls Send-MoeRecordCommit with no `skipped` and no `contested`. A landing whose candidates match the branch tip but which still holds own contested paths therefore gets no daemon MOE_CONTESTED_HELD task line or #governors alert. The session-ended held= line is still posted, because $res.Held is set after attribution.
- The no-candidate send (~4677) omits `contested`, so a strict MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED hold names its peer '?'.
Fix: send the same `skipped` (+$dropped) and `contested` lists as the committed send (~4910). Add a postflight.ps1/.sh regression for an unchanged-tree `nothing` landing with a held contested path. One way to build it: settings.consolidationBranch pre-holding the own file's bytes, with the checkout on main. Found in task-c2a900aa's step-6 review.
definitionOfDone: ps1 MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT (unchanged tree) and no-candidate record_commit carry skipped and contested like sh's record_commit_rpc
postflight.ps1 and postflight.sh assert the record_commit row of an unchanged-tree nothing landing names the held path under its MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED* code

implementationPlan.description:
RED TESTS FIRST (DoD 2): add scenario AI to scripts/tests/postflight.sh and its twin to scripts/tests/postflight.ps1. Model both on scenario AG (sh ~4377, ps1 ~3663) and put each right after scenario AH's 'ok' line.

What AI proves: a held contested path reaches record_commit on BOTH nothing landings.
- The task's only own path is a declared path that is dirty BEFORE pre-flight and also peer-declared, so it is held and nothing lands. This is AG's mechanism: declare_files paths are held by CONTESTED whatever the peer state.
- Use declaredFiles, NOT filesModified. With FAKE_SCOPE_DECLARED_FIELD=1, a filesModified path that is dirty at pre-flight becomes MOE_ATTR_ASSERTED_FOREIGN instead (mem:convention-postflight-scratch-harness).

Three runs:
- AI1, completion (FAKE_TASK_STATUS / -Status REVIEW), default policy, code 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(task-peer)'.
  - Declared count > 0 and nothing missing, so both wrappers enter the build with zero candidates (sh land_commit; ps1 past the no-candidate branch).
  - The tree is unchanged, so this is the ps1 `-not $built.Changed` MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT send.
- AI2, the same with settings {"attribution":{"contested":"skip"}}, code 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED'. The strict code carries no peer, so the daemon names it only from `contested`.
- AI3, checkpoint (status WORKING) with contested=skip. Zero candidates and not a completion, so this is the no-candidate send.

Fixture per run:
- `make_scope_project "$DIR" '[]' <status> '[]' <settings>`. In ps1, New-ScopeProject followed by AG's literal-JSON record write, because PS 5.1 ConvertTo-Json unwraps one-element arrays: `{"id":"task-postflight","title":"Postflight smoke","status":"<status>","filesModified":[],"declaredFiles":["held.txt"]}`.
- COMMIT the rewritten record (`git commit -qm ai-declared .moe/tasks/task-postflight.json`), else it lands as BOARD and the tree changes.
- `echo pre > held.txt`.
- Env: FAKE_SCOPE_DECLARED_FIELD=1 FAKE_SCOPE_PEERS_ACTIVE=1 FAKE_SCOPE_PEER_DECLARED='held.txt:task-peer' FAKE_SCOPE_PEER_ACTIVE=1. In ps1, set them in try and remove them in finally, exactly like AG.
- Run the default no-op CLI: sh `run_scope_wrapper "$DIR" "$out"`; ps1 `Invoke-GateWrapper $dir $out -Status <status>`.

Assertions per run, in both harnesses, each with its own failure message:
(a) the wrapper exits 0;
(b) nothing was committed: `git rev-list --all --count` still equals the fixture's commit count, and held.txt is still untracked and still 'pre';
(c) the LAST record_commit.jsonl row has outcome 'nothing', code 'MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT', and kind 'completion' (AI1, AI2) or 'checkpoint' (AI3);
(d) Array.isArray(row.skipped) && Array.isArray(row.contested). Check this with a node one-liner in both harnesses: the real daemon's readRecordList refuses a non-array with INVALID_INPUT, and a single held path is exactly the one-element case PS 5.1 can mangle;
(e) row.skipped filtered to codes starting 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED' deep-equals [{ path: 'held.txt', code: <run code> }];
(f) row.contested contains { path: 'held.txt', taskId: 'task-peer' };
(g) ps1 only, to prove WHICH send ran: AI1 and AI2 console contains 'the attributable paths already match', and AI3 contains 'no attributable changes to commit'. Match these ASCII substrings only; the console line also holds an em dash in the OEM code page.

If AI1/AI2 do not reach the unchanged-tree line on ps1, switch to the task description's construction. settings.consolidationBranch names a branch made in the fixture holding an owned file's exact bytes, the checkout stays on main/master, and FAKE_CLI_EXTRA_FILE + FILE_CLI write those same bytes during the session. Keep assertion (g).

Bump the commit-scope counters and lists:
- sh: scope_expected_runs 40 to 41 and 39 to 40; add AI to the 'Expected ... scenarios' list.
- ps1: $scopeExpectedRuns 39 to 40 and 40 to 41; add AI to its throw text.

Keep postflight.ps1 UTF-8 with BOM and LF.

RED proof: run the ps1 AI scenario against HEAD's scripts/moe-agent.ps1, either through a trimmed scratch harness or the full harness in a snapshot.
- AI1 and AI2 must fail (e) and (f): no skipped or contested on the unchanged-tree row.
- AI3 must fail (f): no contested on the no-candidate row.
- The sh twin passes on HEAD by design: sh's record_commit_rpc already sends both lists. It is the parity pin.
For a fast sh loop, use the trimmed scratch harness recipe in mem:convention-postflight-scratch-harness, in a snapshot, never the live tree. Record the red output in the step note.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX (DoD 1): every ps1 landing record carries the held lists. Make one helper the single source of the two lists, so the three sends can never drift apart again.

1) scripts/moe-agent.ps1
- Add, next to ConvertTo-MoeRecordPaths (~line 4086), a function, e.g. `Get-MoeRecordHeldFields $Attr $Dropped [string]$Rel`. It returns a hashtable with exactly two keys:
  - `skipped`: @(...) of the non-MOE_ATTR_EXCLUDED $Attr.Skipped entries plus $Dropped, first 100, each @{ path = ConvertTo-MoeRootRelative <Path> $Rel; code = <Code> };
  - `contested`: @(...) of $Attr.Contested, first 100 like the sh twin's contested[:100], each @{ path = ...; taskId = <TaskId> }.
- Filter `$null -ne $_` on both inputs, as the existing landedContested line does. `@($null)` is a one-element array in PowerShell, and a $null $Dropped must not become a bogus entry.
- Comment it as the twin of sh record_commit_rpc's skipped and contested assembly (MOE_ATTR_EXCLUDED skips are static noise that would crowd out the 100 cap).
- Use it at all three sends, by merging into each record with hashtable `+`. The base literal must not already hold either key, because `+` throws on a duplicate key:
  a) the no-candidate send (~4711): pass `@()` as Dropped, since the build has not run and `$dropped` is not yet assigned there. This replaces its inline `skipped` and adds the missing `contested`;
  b) the unchanged-tree `-not $built.Changed` send (~4819): pass `$dropped`. It adds both lists; today it has neither;
  c) the committed `$recArgs` (~4931): pass `$dropped`, replacing its two inline keys. That is behaviour-identical except contested is now capped at 100, as sh caps it.
- Live-launcher safety: every seat in this checkout parses moe-agent.ps1 whole at each launch. Make the change in complete, parseable hunks: the helper first, then each call site. Re-parse after each hunk with `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile`; it must return no errors. Keep the UTF-8 BOM and LF endings (parity-check enforces the BOM).

2) scripts/moe-agent.sh, a one-token parity alignment. The `elif [ "$LAND_OUTCOME" = "nothing" ]` record (~5661) passes "" as record_commit_rpc's 9th argument, DROPPED_FILE. Pass "${LAND_DROPPED_FILE:-}" instead, so an unchanged-tree nothing row carries its staging-time drops exactly like the ps1 row above.
- The no-candidate path still sends none, because run_landing resets LAND_DROPPED_FILE to "" (~5426) and only land_commit sets it (~4688).
- Run `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` before saving the final bytes, since live sh seats hot-reload on change.

Error handling: the sends stay best-effort, so Send-MoeRecordCommit still swallows RPC failures. Empty lists serialize as [] and are accepted by readRecordList.

Re-run the AI scenario (scratch harness, or the full ps1 harness in a snapshot). It must pass on both wrappers.

Contested landing: these four files are also declared by four idle, unassigned WORKING CQ rows (task-16bbf8ff, task-2720c13b, task-7f82e200, task-c4e076cd), and all four were clean at plan time.
- Make every edit through a wrapper-observed file-editing tool call, never a shell cp or redirect onto the live launcher.
- If the session-ended line still reports a path held, say so in the complete_task summary. Never hand-land it.
implementationPlan.note:
scripts/moe-agent.ps1: new Get-MoeRecordHeldFields($Attr, [array]$Dropped, [string]$Rel), placed after ConvertTo-MoeRecordPaths. It returns @{ skipped; contested }:
- skipped: non-EXCLUDED Attr.Skipped plus Dropped, nulls filtered, first 100, {path (root-relative), code};
- contested: Attr.Contested, nulls filtered, first 100, {path, taskId}.
It is merged with hashtable `+` at three sends: no-candidate (Dropped @(); replaces its inline skipped and adds contested), unchanged-tree `-not $built.Changed` (Dropped $dropped; adds both) and committed $recArgs (replaces both inline keys; contested is now capped at 100 like sh). No base literal keeps either key: grep for `skipped =`/`contested =` finds only the helper and unrelated settings/attribution internals.

Edits were made in 4 Edit-tool hunks (helper first), and ParseFile returned 0 errors after each. The UTF-8 BOM and LF endings are kept.

scripts/moe-agent.sh: the nothing record_commit_rpc call's 9th arg changes from "" to "${LAND_DROPPED_FILE:-}". bash -n is OK.

GREEN on snapshot /mnt/d/moe-scratch/ta2f2-green-uVYX (HEAD scripts plus the 4 files), scratch AI harness: sh rc=0, PS 5.1 rc=0, pwsh 7.6.9 rc=0. The PS 5.1 rows now carry skipped [{code,path:held.txt}] and contested [{path:held.txt,taskId:task-peer}] on all three runs, both JSON arrays with one element.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of `git diff -- <4 owned files>` (+147/-18, far under the 400 net-LOC cap). Findings:

- Single source: grep `skipped =` / `contested =` in moe-agent.ps1 finds only the helper, plus unrelated settings (2386/2406) and attribution internals (3618/3620). No inline copy is left at the no-candidate, unchanged-tree or committed sends.
- Duplicate key: no base literal at the 3 merged sends carries skipped or contested, so hashtable `+` cannot throw.
- Edge shapes, run directly under PS 5.1 (AST-extracted helper, ConvertTo-Json -Depth 20 -Compress like Invoke-MoeRpc):
  - $null fields, empty lists, or EXCLUDED-only skips give `"skipped":[]` and `"contested":[]`;
  - one element in each list stays a one-element array of {path,code} / {path,taskId} string objects;
  - 150 entries are capped at 100 in each list;
  - a $null Dropped is filtered, and one dropped entry is kept;
  - Rel 'sub/' is stripped from the paths.
- Exit paths: the helper is pure. There is no StrictMode or global Stop EAP, and $attr always has Skipped/Contested arrays (single construction at ~3762). The new list-building on the nothing paths therefore cannot throw into the landing catch.
- sh: run_landing resets LAND_DROPPED_FILE to "" and only land_commit sets it. The no-candidate and BOARD-deferral nothing rows are byte-identical to before; only an unchanged-tree nothing row gains its staging drops (recs() also tolerates a missing file). bash -n is clean.
- BOM and LF are kept in moe-agent.ps1 and postflight.ps1; parity-check.sh, PS 5.1 and pwsh are all green.
- Non-vacuity: AI pins outcome, code and kind (c), array shape (d) and, on ps1, the branch console line (g). RED on HEAD failed AI1-AI3 exactly at (d).
- Governor visibility: recordCommit.ts heldContestedPaths reads the CONTESTED* skip codes and takes a strict hold's peer from contested. alertGovernors fires on held.length>0 even for outcome nothing. A ps1 unchanged-tree held path now yields MOE_CONTESTED_HELD and the #governors alert, and AI2 names its peer instead of '?'.
- Residual, out of DoD and filed as task-dfbda1a8230a4fe5b57dbe512fa62a33 (LOW, dependsOn this task): the ps1 failed sends (peel/build/gate/commit/ref-contention/teardown), the Invoke-MoeRescueRef kind=rescue send and the catch/finally post-CAS committed re-sends still omit both lists. sh's record_commit_rpc sends them on every outcome.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Every ps1 landing record that follows attribution (committed, the unchanged-tree MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, and the no-candidate nothing/refused) sends `skipped` (non-MOE_ATTR_EXCLUDED skips plus staging drops, at most 100) and `contested` (at most 100), as sh's record_commit_rpc does. A held contested path on an unchanged-tree landing therefore raises the daemon's MOE_CONTESTED_HELD task line and #governors alert, and a strict hold names its real peer instead of '?'. sh's nothing record also carries the unchanged-tree drops, so both wrappers send identical lists.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
CHOSEN: one ps1 helper (Get-MoeRecordHeldFields or similar) that builds `skipped` and `contested` for the committed, unchanged-tree nothing and no-candidate sends. The task asks for 'the same lists as the committed send', and a shared helper makes that structural.

Drops: the description says skipped includes $dropped. sh's nothing record passes no DROPPED_FILE today, so a ps1-only change would make the wrappers diverge on the rare unchanged-tree-with-drops landing. The one-token sh alignment keeps them identical.

- Inlining the lists at two more sites: a third and fourth copy is how this gap arose.
- Fixing the failed-outcome sends too: outside the DoD. Note it as a residual gap.

Test construction: AI1/AI2 reach the unchanged-tree branch without the consolidationBranch trick. A completion whose only own path is a held declared path enters the build with zero candidates (sh: completion && ATTR_N_DECLARED > 0 && not all missing; ps1: past the no-candidate branch because AssertedCount > 0). - Contested landing: the four files are declared by four idle CQ rows. Use a wrapper-observed editing tool.
- The harnesses are long: postflight.sh takes about 12+ min on WSL Linux and about 1h45m on Git Bash; postflight.ps1 about 10-12 min on PS 5.1. Run them in the background against a /mnt/d snapshot.
